items.title: Stale repository / reference state
items.summary: A local checkout or local origin/main ref lags the remote, and conclusions are drawn from the stale view: a diff appears to contain other sessions' work, or a present file is read as absent.

evidence_refs.note: INC-002A-F1-001/002/003; three independently evidenced incidents
GA-HIST-04 witnesses a stale base SHA and broken ancestry as a recorded failure class
002A section 6 records this family as recurrent at 3 eligible incidents

current_controls: git fetch origin <branch> before any origin/main diff or file-absence conclusion
git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main
Grounding repo_head / file_exists claims whose expected values are sourced outside the stale checkout
Grounding fixtures GA-HIST-01, GA-HIST-03, GA-HIST-04
items.control_gap: Grounding resolves repo_head local-first, so a stale local origin/main that still resolves is trusted. Detection requires an expected SHA or path sourced from outside that stale view; a claim authored from the stale checkout MATCHes. No control compares local origin/main to GitHub main when the local ref resolves.
items.agent_required_basis: 002A section 10 records the family as covered by procedure and by Grounding when invoked; a freshness comparison is a small deterministic check, not an authority boundary.
open_questions: Should the local-vs-remote freshness comparison live in Grounding as a claim type, or as a standalone pre-flight utility?
Would it be advisory, or would a divergence be a STOP?
deployment_gates: Recurrence established: at least two independent census incidents (satisfied, 3)
Owner decides between a Grounding claim type and a standalone check
Confirm the check cannot itself be authored from the stale view

items.title: Inherited claim epistemic drift
items.summary: A cross-session handoff carries claims forward while the evidence behind them is left behind. The claims are then adopted as premises without re-derivation.

evidence_refs.note: INC-002A-F3-001, the only escaped incident in the 002A census
the transferable rule: a cross-session handoff preserves claims, not their epistemic status
5 inherited claims re-derived, 2 refuted

current_controls: The written re-derivation rule in the reconciliation artifact
Dev Order practice of re-deriving load-bearing inherited claims
Grounding v0.2 handoff_provenance claim (checks declared lane provenance, not claim content)
items.control_gap: Grounding verifies repository state and, since v0.2, declared lane provenance. Neither checks claim *content*: there is still no evidence-reattachment claim type, so an inherited claim can survive a PROCEED. Whether the written re-derivation rule is operationally sufficient as a standing control is not demonstrated.
items.agent_required_basis: Singular incident. 002A section 11 records that a Reconciliation or Evidence agent would re-open Grounding's question or become an extension of it.
open_questions: v0.2 added handoff_provenance but deliberately not a content claim. Is a content/evidence-reattachment claim type the right shape for v0.3, or does it exceed a grounding agent's authority?
Can 'this claim's evidence was re-acquired' be checked deterministically at all?
deployment_gates: A second independent epistemic-drift incident, not from the PR #339 audit cluster (002A falsifier 2)
Evidence that the written re-derivation rule alone does not prevent recurrence

items.title: False-absence findings
items.summary: A search that returns nothing is treated as proof of absence. 002A excluded this family because no documented case was available to it; that exclusion was correct on the evidence 002A held. This pass recovered two durable instances, which supersede that evidentiary state.

evidence_refs.note: BR-024 adjudicated SUPERSEDED: grep-absence of the literal ezdxf.new(R2000) call form was read as R2000 removal; R2000 remains supported across ~29 app/ files
inherited claim 'Step 0 is RED because svgwrite is absent' REFUTED; svgwrite is declared and installed by sandbox CI
GA-HIST-02 reports a missing path as environment-scoped absence, not 'never existed'

current_controls: docs/audit/PIXEL_PLATFORM_LOOP1_FORENSIC_AUDIT.md:438 — no state is assigned from grep-absence alone
Grounding reports environment-scoped absence rather than non-existence (GA-HIST-02)
items.control_gap: The grep-absence rule is stated in one audit's method section, not in repository-wide governance, and nothing enforces it. Both recovered instances predate it. Its reach beyond that audit is unestablished.
items.agent_required_basis: Not analysed for agent necessity: the item cannot reach readiness until its evidence is ratified into the census.
open_questions: Are BR-024 and the svgwrite refutation independent underlying incidents? They arose in different subsystems at different times, but the svgwrite refutation shares a discovery event with INC-002A-F3-001.
Should the grep-absence rule be promoted from one audit's method section to repository-wide governance?
deployment_gates: Census admission: an owner-authorized reconciliation admitting these instances into the incident census
Recurrence established from at least two independent census incidents after admission

items.title: Grounding GitHub evidence blocked when only the gh CLI is authenticated
items.summary: Grounding's GitHub adapter reads GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN from the environment only. An operator authenticated solely through the gh CLI keyring gets BLOCKED on every pr_state claim, and a BLOCKED run is a STOP decision.

evidence_refs.note: BLOCKED / STOP at b53f9963: 15 checked, 13 matched, 2 blocked — both pr_state claims, message 'no GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN available for GitHub read'. Re-run with the token exported returned MATCH / PROCEED 15/15, isolating credentials as the sole cause.
token read from os.environ only; no gh CLI path, by the adapter's no-subprocess design

current_controls: The adapter fails closed: it returns BLOCKED rather than silently proceeding without GitHub evidence
items.control_gap: Operability, not correctness. The prerequisite is not stated where an operator would see it before a run, so a correct fail-closed STOP is indistinguishable at first sight from a real divergence.
items.agent_required_basis: A gh CLI fallback is constitutionally forbidden — the adapter's read-only guarantee rests on having no subprocess path. The remaining fix is documenting the environment prerequisite.
open_questions: Should the CLI name the missing environment variable as a setup prerequisite in its BLOCKED message?
Should the trial ledger distinguish 'blocked on operator environment' from 'blocked on an unavailable evidence source'?
deployment_gates: Census admission: an owner-authorized reconciliation admitting this into the incident census
Confirm no fix is attempted that introduces a shell-out path into the adapter
